data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2017 gross claims outstanding were GBP 399.227m. The year saw significant catastrophe activity in the second half (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria, Mexico Earthquake and California Wildfires) which materially impacted the Syndicate's loss ratio and increased claims outstanding and IBNR; the managing agent reports net unfavourable development on prior accident year losses (net GBP 25.7m). Reinsurers' share of claims outstanding also increased markedly due to recoveries from the catastrophe losses and quota-share reinsurance arrangements. Overall the report describes adverse prior year development driven by catastrophe losses and related reserve increases, particularly in property-related lines, with additional impacts from casualty quota-share IBNR increases and reinsurance recovery volatility.
raw_causal_phrases: The result for the year included net unfavourable development on prior accident year losses of GBP 25.7m (2016 - GBP 2.3m favourable development).

The net loss ratio for the year was 82.0% (2016 - 53.8%). The loss ratio was significantly impacted by the losses from the catastrophe events during the second half of the year which included Hurricane Harvey, Hurricane Irma, Hurricane Maria, Mexico Earthquake and the California Wildfires.

Reinsurers' share of claims outstanding as at 31 December 2017 is GBP 330.8m compared to GBP 62.6m as at the prior year. The increase in reinsurers' share of claims outstanding is primarily due to recoveries from the Syndicate's catastrophe losses in the year and increasing IBNR from the casualty quota share contracts in line with the growth in the underlying assumed casualty book.

Gross technical provisions have increased to GBP 967.6m from GBP 600.6m. This is driven by an increase in claims outstanding, principally as IBNR, primarily attributed to the catastrophe losses incurred during the second half of the year.
